item.title: Koroilavesau calls to tap forest carbon market
item.description: FIJI is leaving a major forest carbon opportunity untapped as other countries move ahead with climate finance and carbon investment, says Opposition member Semi Koroilavesau. item.content:encoded:
FIJI is leaving a major forest carbon opportunity untapped as other countries move ahead with climate finance and carbon investment, says Opposition member Semi Koroilavesau.

Speaking in Parliament, Mr Koroilavesau said Fiji had about 70,000 hectares of mahogany plantations, one of the largest tropical hardwood plantation areas in the world, but had failed to develop a comprehensive strategy to quantify and monetise their carbon potential.

He said countries were generating investment and climate finance through well-managed forest carbon programs while Fiji continued to lag behind.

Mr Koroilavesau said Government needed to strengthen forest carbon accounting and reforestation while creating policies that allow indigenous forests and commercial plantations to contribute to Fiji’s national emissions reduction commitments.

“Instead of relying solely on international climate leadership, Government should demonstrate that leadership here at home,” he said.

He said proper management of the forestry sector could protect biodiversity, create sustainable livelihoods for rural communities and generate revenue through carbon markets.

Mr Koroilavesau urged Government to develop a comprehensive forestry roadmap bringing together Agarwood, mahogany, indigenous forests, sustainable harvesting, carbon sequestration and climate finance.

He said Fiji must stop viewing forests only as timber resources and recognise their wider economic and environmental value.

item.title: 160-plus communities seek coastal protection
item.description: MORE than 160 coastal communities across Fiji have sought Government assistance for coastal protection, far exceeding the resources currently available, Parliament was told yesterday. Minister for Information, Environment and Climate Change Lynda Tabuya said there were currently no confirmed seawall or coastal protection construction projects for the Lau Group in the 2026-2027 financial year.
item.content:encoded:
MORE than 160 coastal communities across Fiji have sought Government assistance for coastal protection, far exceeding the resources currently available, Parliament was told yesterday.

Minister for Information, Environment and Climate Change Lynda Tabuya said there were currently no confirmed seawall or coastal protection construction projects for the Lau Group in the 2026-2027 financial year.

However, she said Lau was not being overlooked, with Government actively pursuing climate finance to support vulnerable communities.

Discussions are underway for a nature-based seawall on Ogea Island in the Tikina of Fulaga, while Waciwaci, Avea and Lomaloma have been included among 43 communities prioritised for detailed climate risk assessments.

The assessments will determine whether communities can be protected through seawalls and other adaptation measures, or whether relocation may eventually be necessary.

Ms Tabuya said Fiji had secured $5.7million through the Adaptation Fund for nature-based seawalls, with about 4.3 kilometres planned across 14 high-risk communities in Macuata, Cakaudrove, Nadroga/Navosa, Ra and Lomaiviti.

She said relocation remained the last option, with Government first seeking ways to help communities remain safely on their land.

On Waciwaci, Ms Tabuya said the assessment would also determine whether the village school needed to be relocated, in consultation with the Ministry of Education.

item.title: Sole trader asset declarations deadline deferred – Minister
item.description: THE mandatory asset declaration regime for registered sole traders has been deferred until January 1, 2027, Parliament was told yesterday. Finance Minister Esrom Immanuel said the measure was delayed to allow the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS) more time to develop and test the system.
item.content:encoded:
THE mandatory asset declaration regime for registered sole traders has been deferred until January 1, 2027, Parliament was told yesterday.

Finance Minister Esrom Immanuel said the measure was delayed to allow the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS) more time to develop and test the system.

A public notice issued in February informed taxpayers that implementation would be deferred to a subsequent filing period.

Mr Immanuel said two rounds of stakeholder consultations had been conducted following the Budget announcement, with feedback used to refine the framework and ensure the requirements were practical and proportionate.

The regime will require affected sole traders to declare specified assets through FRCS’s online tax system when filing their tax returns.

Mr Immanuel said the information would help FRCS strengthen tax compliance and transparency, particularly by identifying inconsistencies between declared income, business activities and asset positions that may require further review.

He said there would be no additional financial cost to sole traders, although they would have an additional compliance requirement during implementation.

FRCS plans to conduct a stakeholder awareness and education program in the final quarter of this year to ensure taxpayers understand the requirements before the regime takes effect.

item.content:encoded:
MINISTER for Education Aseri Radrodro has urged schools to use assessment results to identify learning gaps and provide targeted support to students, saying student learning remains the ministry’s main priority.

Speaking at the 43rd Fiji Head Teachers Association’s annual conference in Nadi yesterday, he said the 2026 Literacy and Numeracy Assessment (LANA) had been conducted, with results expected to provide further insight into student performance.

He said changes were also being made to the national examination system, with scaling of marks to begin in 2026 following a Cabinet decision. The Year 8 Examination will be held in week five of Term Three, and heads of schools were urged to ensure students are well prepared through completion of teaching programs and additional support for those struggling.

Mr Radrodro said scaling would form part of the assessment process, but students must still demonstrate learning.

item.title: $200 fine ‘toothless’ without enforcement
item.description: THE Opposition has backed the Government’s push for a cleaner Fiji, but questioned whether the planned $200 littering fine is evidence-based, fairly applied and supported by enough enforcement and waste infrastructure. Opposition MP Virendra Lal raised the concerns in Parliament this week in response to Environment Minister Lynda Tabuya’s ministerial statement on the Government’s strengthened litt
item.content:encoded:
THE Opposition has backed the Government’s push for a cleaner Fiji, but questioned whether the planned $200 littering fine is evidence-based, fairly applied and supported by enough enforcement and waste infrastructure.

Opposition MP Virendra Lal raised the concerns in Parliament this week in response to Environment Minister Lynda Tabuya’s ministerial statement on the Government’s strengthened litter enforcement measures.

Mr Lal questioned the basis for increasing the fixed penalty from $40 to $200.

“I ask the minister, where is the evidence base for that figure? Was this number modelled against comparable jurisdictions, or arrived at by other means?,” Mr Lal asked.

He said a flat $200 penalty could disproportionately affect low-income Fijians.

“And critically, has the ministry considered what a flat $200 fine actually means across our population?

“For a struggling family, a market vendor, or a young person, $200 is a significant and punishing summer.”

Mr Lal also questioned whether the Government had enough officers, resources and infrastructure to enforce the new penalty, particularly in rural and maritime communities.

“A fine only deters if people believe they will be caught.

“Without genuine enforcement capacity behind it, a fivefold penalty increase risk being nothing more than a number on paper, tough in the press release, toothless on the street.”

He said Government must invest in prevention, including bins, collection services and public education.

“Because punishing littering without giving people somewhere else to put their rubbish does not change behaviour, it simply criminalises the absence of infrastructure.”

Mr Lal called for the draft litter regulations, National Integrated Waste Management and Pollution Control Strategy and its Implementation Plan to be tabled before Parliament for scrutiny.

item.title: Students miss out Year 8 exams
item.description: A total of 372 Year 8 students registered for the 2025 external examination did not sit the exam, raising concerns over student attendance and prompting Education Minister Aseri Radrodro to call for urgent action. Of the 19,000 students registered, 18,628 sat the examination, with the Ministry of Education now investigating why the remaining students were absent.
item.content:encoded:
A total of 372 Year 8 students registered for the 2025 external examination did not sit the exam, raising concerns over student attendance and prompting Education Minister Aseri Radrodro to call for urgent action.

Of the 19,000 students registered, 18,628 sat the examination, with the Ministry of Education now investigating why the remaining students were absent.

Speaking at the 43rd Fiji Head Teachers Association’s annual conference in Nadi yesterday, Mr Radrodro said the recently passed Education Act 2026 strengthened the framework for compulsory education and reinforced the importance of regular attendance.

He urged schools to identify attendance problems early and work with parents and the ministry to address the causes before prolonged absences affected students’ learning.

Student and teacher attendance are among several issues being discussed at the three-day conference, alongside drugs, bullying, health and student safety.

Mr Radrodro urged head teachers to ensure Year 8 students and their parents were aware of technical and vocational education and training (TVET) pathways available from Year 9.

item.title: Ministry to redeploy surplus teachers
item.description: THE Ministry of Education will redeploy surplus teachers to schools with genuine staffing shortages before considering further recruitment, says Education Minister Aseri Radrodro. Speaking at the 43rd Fiji Head Teachers Association’s annual conference in Nadi yesterday, Mr Radrodro acknowledged association president Johnson Rura for raising concerns about teacher shortages.
item.content:encoded:
THE Ministry of Education will redeploy surplus teachers to schools with genuine staffing shortages before considering further recruitment, says Education Minister Aseri Radrodro.

Speaking at the 43rd Fiji Head Teachers Association’s annual conference in Nadi yesterday, Mr Radrodro acknowledged association president Johnson Rura for raising concerns about teacher shortages.

He said the ministry was reviewing teachers already employed across the country, including their qualifications, locations and the staffing needs of schools.

“Teachers may be required to undertake ministerial transfers where there is a staffing need,” Mr Radrodro said.

He said the redeployment exercise would ensure existing teachers were used effectively before the ministry considered recruiting additional teachers.

Mr Radrodro also stressed the importance of accurate ER5 staffing information in making decisions about teacher deployment and recruitment.

He said the ministry had identified cases where ER5 information did not accurately reflect the number of teachers available in schools or divisions.

“You know who you are, and you need to improve on the quality and the accuracy of data that you fill in your ER5.”

Mr Radrodro said the ministry was also checking ER5 information against records in the Fiji Education Management Information System (FEMIS) to verify staffing data.

He said the verification process was intended to ensure schools provided accurate information to support staffing and recruitment decisions.

item.title: Absence issue flagged
item.description: SOME teachers have recorded more than 100 days of absence, prompting the Ministry of Education to strengthen its monitoring of teacher attendance. Education Minister Aseri Radrodro said the cases were identified through the recent Fiji Education Staffing Appointment (FESA) system-cleaning exercise.
item.content:encoded:
SOME teachers have recorded more than 100 days of absence, prompting the Ministry of Education to strengthen its monitoring of teacher attendance.

Education Minister Aseri Radrodro said the cases were identified through the recent Fiji Education Staffing Appointment (FESA) system-cleaning exercise.

Speaking at the 43rd Fiji Head Teachers Association’s annual conference in Nadi yesterday, Mr Radrodro said each case would be assessed through the appropriate process, taking into account approved leave and other legitimate circumstances.

He said prolonged teacher absences could disrupt school operations and affect student learning, while accurate attendance records could also help determine whether reported staffing shortages were genuine.

The minister urged schools to maintain proper attendance records and refer relevant cases to the ministry’s human resources department.

He said the ministry was also addressing issues involving teacher appointments, transfers, vacancies, payroll and acting allowances.

Some teachers, he said, had started work while waiting for salaries or acting allowances to be processed, while delays in receiving teachers’ bank details had also affected payments. The ministry is working with the ministries of Civil Service and Finance to resolve the issues.

Mr Radrodro said vacancies and restrictions on appointments needed to be carefully assessed, particularly where teachers could be redeployed to meet staffing needs elsewhere.

He urged stakeholders to ensure all vacant positions were advertised and filled before the end of the year.
